title: Personal OKR weekly retro - week of 2026-03-09
content:
Weekly check-in / quick retro (notes to self)

Context:
- Role: SWE on serving-runtime (latency/cost work).
- OKR focus Q1: reduce tail latency for hosted API and increase throughput for smaller batch workloads.
- This doc = personal scratchpad for KPIs, progress, blockers, and next-week plan.

KPI snapshot (current vs target) - quick numbers to track:
- 95th percentile token-generation latency (prod hosted v2): 210ms -> target 170ms by end of Q1 (still behind).
- P50 latency: 42ms -> target 35ms.
- Cost-per-1k-tokens (inference infra): $0.38 -> target $0.30 (planned quant + batching).
- Throughput for small-batch (N=1-4): 220 req/s -> target 300 req/s for dedicated profiles.
- Eval quality regressions: 0 major regressions this sprint (good).

What I shipped this week:
- Benchmarked Llama-2-Chat quantized path on A100 and M40 sims (notes in PR 987). Results show ~12% p50 improvement for 4k contexts when enabling kernel X.
- Small refactor to continuous-batching scheduler (reduce lock contention) - landed on dev, running smoke.
- Added extra tracing tags for route+model variant to help debug routing-induced lat spikes.

Observed wins / surprises:
- Kernel X yields better throughput only for sequence lengths > 1024. For short seqs (<512) it regresses latency slightly. Need auto-routing rule.
- Tracing revealed one route mis-classified as high-priority causing suboptimal batching; created ticket CON-ENG-5021.

Blockers / concerns:
- Perf regression in canary after refactor (95p spiking at certain times). Probably KV-cache invalidation edge case when we preempt batches.
- Need infra time to repro the spike under load - SRE alignment required. Pinged Maya.
- Quantized model accuracy for a subset of prompts shows ~0.7% BLEU-like metric drop; evaluate if acceptable for customer tiers. Samira to run eval set.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Should we enable Kernel X only for model variants pinned to longer sequences? (Proposal: route based on sequence length histogram + model.arch tag).
- Rollback plan for refactor if canary regression persists? Time-windowed rollback with auto-fallback to previous scheduler config.

Action items (owner, due):
- Ethan: Add auto-routing rule prototype for kernel X (WIP) - due 2026-03-14.
- Maya: Help repro 95p spike under synthetic load, provide flame graphs - due 2026-03-12.
- Samira: Finish eval suite run for quantized models and summarise quality delta - due 2026-03-13.
- Ethan: Add metrics dashboard tile for seq-length conditioned latency (short/medium/long) - due 2026-03-15.

Risks / mitigation:
- If we enable kernel X globally, short workloads will regress - mitigation: phased rollout by model variant and seq-length routing + canary with traffic split.
- Cost reduction via quantization might impact quality for some prompts - mitigation: tier-based serving (dedicated customers get higher-precision variants) and opt-in flag for risky workloads.

Personal reflections / retrospective notes:
- I spent too much time debugging infra flakes this week; need to carve dedicated deep work blocks.
- Better to ship a smaller, safer routing change with observability hooks than a big refactor without canarying.
- Need to lean on Maya earlier for load repro instead of iterating locally.

Next week plan (top priorities):
1) Prototype seq-length routing rule and smoke end-to-end with kernel X only for long sequences. (Ethan)
2) Reproduce 95p spike under controlled load and get SRE on-call to triage. (Maya+Ethan)
3) Finalize quant eval and decide on gradated rollout for quantized variants. (Samira + Ethan)
4) Dashboard: add seq-length conditioned latency tile and per-route kernel assignment trace.

Quick notes / scratchpad:
- Related PRs: #987 (kernel perf), #992 (batcher refactor), link to local perf logs: /mnt/efs/perf/2026-03-09/*.log
- Slack threads: #serving-runtime (see thread pinned about kernel X), #perf-daily.
- Confluence: perf playbook (internal) for reproducing latency spikes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Perf+Playbook

TODO (short):
- [ ] push auto-routing prototype to branch -> draft PR
- [ ] add dashboard tile + alert if 95p > 180ms for short seqs
- [ ] schedule 1:1 with Maya to sync on repro plan

Notes to self: keep changelogs small and add rollback markers, instrument every change with route+kernel tags.

End of weekly scratchpad.
summary: Personal weekly OKR/retro scratchpad for Ethan Morales covering KPI numbers, shipped work, blockers, actions, and next-week priorities.
